page: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-22-standardlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 22 dedicated vCPUs across 11 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. The x86_64 CPU features 105 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets. System memory totals 176 GB of RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive enterprise tasks without dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Local persistent I/O is backed by 6442 GB of NVMe SSD storage distributed over two local drives. Memory bandwidth testing demonstrates cached read throughput of 1495.22 GB/sec and uncached read throughput of 99.03 GB/sec, combined with write speeds of 42.11 GB/sec. Across compute and application benchmarks, the instance delivers balanced multi-core execution, registering a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 119.03 GB/sec and 23.89 million Redis SET operations per second.

Hardware tradeoffs focus on high disk density and memory allocations over maximum single-thread compute velocities. CPU PassMark scores of 27968.71 and Geekbench multi-core ratings of 11688 place it within median performance distributions. The configuration offers strong resource density for disk-bound caching clusters, relational database management systems, real-time analytics engines, and transactional datastores requiring low-latency NVMe scratch space.
description: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-22-standardlssd is a storage-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz with 22 dedicated vCPUs and 176 GB of RAM. Designed for heavy data pipelines, it includes 6442 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across two drives, while omitting dedicated GPUs. The system balances 8 GB of memory per core with high-capacity local disk bandwidth, supporting sustained memory read operations up to 99.03 GB/sec and cached reads reaching 1495.22 GB/sec. Synthetic and application benchmarks show steady median results across computational tests alongside 23.89 million Redis SET operations per second and 119.03 GB/sec multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The resource combination presents cost-effective utility for workloads dominated by active working sets and rapid local storage access, making it appropriate for distributed database nodes, in-memory caching platforms, and operational data stores requiring low-latency scratch drives.
